title: Business Acquisition
uncertainty_note: Editorial sensitivity band, not a statistical interval. Confidence is a supplied classification; independent source review is required.

score_rationale.revenue_potential: Revenue Potential: 24/25. Existing cash flow requires purchase capital, retained staff and debt-service discipline.
score_rationale.profit_margin_potential: Profit Margin Potential: 16/25. Existing cash flow requires purchase capital, retained staff and debt-service discipline.
score_rationale.team_efficiency: Team Efficiency: 7/20. Existing cash flow requires purchase capital, retained staff and debt-service discipline.
score_rationale.startup_accessibility: Startup Accessibility: 2/15. Existing cash flow requires purchase capital, retained staff and debt-service discipline.
score_rationale.automation_potential: Automation Potential: 8/15. Existing cash flow requires purchase capital, retained staff and debt-service discipline.

economics.owner_net_profit_potential: $60,000–$540,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment
economics.includes_contractors_note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.
economics.revenue_basis: Acquired business sales; margin after interest, before principal repayments
economics.cost_basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.
economics.estimate_status: Illustrative assumptions; not verified earnings data

conservative.assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.

base_case.assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.

scaled_small_team.assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.

regulatory_notes: Review employment, tax, licenses, lender covenants and transaction disclosures.

plays.name: Distressed Asset Recovery
plays.mechanism: Locate mispriced, orphaned, or administratively stranded assets—tax-sale overages, unclaimed state funds, dormant judgments, government surplus lots, or distressed micro-businesses—and capture a contingent recovery fee or acquisition spread.
inputs: Tax-sale excess proceeds ledgers
Unclaimed property & judgment dockets
Surplus auction manifests
workflow: Audit statutory fee caps, claim windows, and chain-of-title encumbrances
Execute skip-tracing or asset inspection to confirm net realizable value
Lock in contingent recovery agreements or below-intrinsic buyouts
metrics: Gross spread / contingent fee per case
Claim approval rate
Days from filing to disbursement

platform_risks.failure_mode: Statutory fee-cap compression or administrative hold
platform_risks.trigger: Jurisdiction updates finder fee limits, waiting periods, or filing documentation rules
platform_risks.impact: Reduced net fee margin or extended cash conversion cycle
platform_risks.detection_metric: County/state rejection notice rate and days-to-payout variance
platform_risks.fallback: Diversify across multi-state dockets and use attorney-backed filing partnerships where required

plays.name: Dormant Chrome Extension & Shopify App Roll-Up / Monetization Flip
plays.mechanism: Scan the Chrome Web Store, WordPress Plugin Directory, and Shopify App Store for high-install (10,000–250,000 active users), 4.5+-star free utilities neglected by solo developers, acquire them at 1–2x potential annual cashflow, and introduce clean freemium Pro tiers or opt-in contextual partner offers.
inputs: Chrome Web Store / Shopify / WP plugin scraper filtering by active installs, rating, & last-updated date (>12 months)
Asset Purchase Agreement (APA) & Chrome Web Store developer-account transfer checklist
Freemium Stripe checkout SDK + non-intrusive opt-in partner recommendation module
workflow: Identify utility extensions and micro-apps with strong organic weekly installs and zero monetization whose solo creator has not pushed an update in 12–24 months
Acquire the codebase, store listing, and domain for $3,000–$35,000 with an escrowed transfer through the official developer console
Ship a Manifest V3 maintenance update first to build user trust, then grandfather existing free features while adding a $7–$19/mo Pro power-user tier or explicit opt-in partner deals
metrics: Acquisition payback period (target 2–5 months)
Free-to-Pro conversion rate (1.5–4%) + monthly ARPU per 1,000 WAU
Post-acquisition review rating stability (>=4.4 stars) and uninstall rate (<3%)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Chrome Web Store malware/policy takedown or mass 1-star user revolt after acquisition
platform_risks.trigger: Injecting silent background adware/tracking scripts post-acquisition or locking previously free core features behind a sudden paywall
platform_risks.impact: Permanent Chrome Web Store removal and total write-off of acquisition capital
platform_risks.detection_metric: Zero CWS permission-scope expansion without user opt-in and daily 1-star review velocity monitor
platform_risks.fallback: Never inject hidden tracking or background ad scripts; keep existing permissions narrow, grandfather all legacy free features, and monetize strictly via additive Pro workflows

plays.name: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Schedule E/F Trade-Claim & Convenience-Class Rollups
plays.mechanism: Purchase documented small trade claims below risk-adjusted expected plan distributions, accounting for objections, assignment procedures, and plan rules that may prohibit claim splitting or aggregation benefits.
inputs: Bankruptcy schedules E/F and claims register
Invoices, payment history, and assignment documents
Proposed plan classification and distribution waterfall
workflow: 1. Reconcile scheduled trade creditors with filed claims and supporting invoices
2. Model recoveries under plan amendments, objections, setoffs, and convenience-class eligibility
3. Buy eligible claims through documented assignments and complete required transfer notices
4. Monitor objections and confirmation, then reconcile distributions to each acquired claim
metrics: Purchase discount to risk-adjusted recovery
Allowed claim value versus purchased face value
Realized return and days to distribution

platform_risks.trigger: Disputed invoices, setoff rights, or plan restrictions on purchased or split claims
platform_risks.impact: Reduced distribution or complete capital loss
platform_risks.detection_metric: Objection rate and eligible allowed value per portfolio
platform_risks.fallback: Stop affected purchases, enforce documented seller recourse where available, and price only supported general-unsecured recoveries

plays.name: Aged Shelf-Corp Reinstatement, Primary Tradeline & 0%-APR Corporate Credit Stacking
plays.mechanism: Compare reinstated entities and genuine business credit facilities for working-capital financing; entity age is not operating history, and promotional APR economics require accurate underwriting and repayment capacity.
inputs: Entity filings, beneficial ownership, and liability searches
Verified operating financials and genuine supplier tradelines
Lender eligibility, promotional APR, fee, and guarantee terms
workflow: 1. Audit the entity's ownership, tax liabilities, and reinstatement requirements
2. Disclose acquisition and actual operating history; establish only genuine paid supplier accounts
3. Compare lender-approved applications with full debt disclosure and consolidated exposure limits
4. Fund documented business expenses and repay before promotional expiry using cash-flow reserves
metrics: Effective borrowing cost including fees
Debt service coverage under post-promotion APR
Utilization and days to promotional expiry

platform_risks.trigger: Misstated operating history, undisclosed debt, or expired promotional terms
platform_risks.impact: Account closure, accelerated repayment, and guarantee exposure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Underwriting discrepancies and stressed repayment coverage
platform_risks.fallback: Halt applications, correct disclosures, and use a transparent term facility or reduce financed spending

plays.name: FERC / ISO Substation Interconnection Queue & Powered-Land Option Flipping
plays.mechanism: Overlay public interconnection queues with land-use and substation data to option potentially useful sites, treating queue position and nearby infrastructure as signals rather than guaranteed deliverable power.
inputs: ISO and utility interconnection queues and study results
Parcel zoning, transmission corridors, and substation maps
Utility service estimates and developer site requirements
workflow: 1. Match queue activity and infrastructure constraints to suitable parcels
2. Verify site control requirements, zoning, environmental limits, and utility capacity assumptions
3. Negotiate assignable diligence-contingent options within capped carrying-cost budgets
4. Assign approved options to qualified developers with explicit disclosure of unresolved power and study conditions
metrics: Option cost per qualified developable acre
Utility-validated capacity versus marketed capacity
Net assignment proceeds after study and option costs

platform_risks.failure_mode: Queue withdrawal or prohibitive network upgrade cost
platform_risks.trigger: Restudy, milestone failure, or capacity estimate unsupported by utility commitments
platform_risks.impact: Option expiry and unrecoverable diligence spending
platform_risks.detection_metric: Study cost revisions and unresolved interconnection milestones
platform_risks.fallback: Let contingent options lapse or reposition land for independently viable uses without claiming secured power

plays.name: Automated Form 8850 WOTC (Work Opportunity Tax Credit) & Section 41 R&D Contingency Engine
plays.mechanism: Automate employer-authorized WOTC screening and separately substantiate Section 41 research credits, earning outcome-linked service fees only where permitted; program authorization, qualifying activities, wage coordination, and professional fee restrictions govern each claim.
inputs: Consented hiring records, Form 8850 responses, and payroll hours
Research project evidence and qualified expense ledgers
State workforce certification procedures and tax-year credit and fee rules
workflow: 1. Confirm WOTC authorization for each hire date and complete required prescreening by the job-offer date
2. Submit Form 8850 and required supporting forms within the applicable 28-day deadline and track state certification and qualifying hours
3. Separately document Section 41 qualifying research and expenses, reconciling wage overlap and applicable deduction adjustments with a tax professional
4. Obtain employer and preparer approval before filing, retain audit support, and collect permitted fees without guaranteeing credits
metrics: Timely WOTC certification submission rate
Substantiated credits realized by the employer
Net permitted service fees after review and filing costs

platform_risks.failure_mode: Credit denial or impermissible contingent-fee arrangement
platform_risks.trigger: Expired program authority, late certification, unsupported research expenses, or restricted practitioner compensation
platform_risks.impact: Reduced credits, amended returns, penalties, and fee repayment exposure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Deadline exceptions, certification denials, and unsupported expense share
platform_risks.fallback: Exclude unsupported claims and use compliant fixed-fee payroll and research-documentation services under independent tax review

plays.name: Commercial Solar Tax-Equity Flip & Bonus-Depreciation Strip Syndication
plays.mechanism: Arrange commercial solar partnership-flip investments that allocate supported tax benefits and cash flows to genuine equity owners; depreciation cannot be sold as a standalone credit, and allocations require economic substance, tax compliance, and securities-law review.
inputs: Solar project costs, ownership records, and operating contracts
Investor tax capacity and dated depreciation eligibility analysis
Counsel-reviewed partnership waterfall and securities offering documents
workflow: 1. Underwrite project cash flows, eligible basis, construction and service dates, and current credit and depreciation availability
2. Verify investor suitability, tax capacity, at-risk and passive-loss limits, and applicable securities and intermediary requirements
3. Structure counsel-approved partnership allocations and flip terms with genuine equity risk, basis adjustments, and recapture protections
4. Close through authorized intermediaries and monitor operations, tax reporting, and flip conditions before distributing permitted fees
metrics: Qualified tax-equity capital closed
Realized investor distributions versus underwritten waterfall
Net permitted placement fees after legal and diligence costs

platform_risks.failure_mode: Tax allocations disallowed or unlicensed securities placement
platform_risks.trigger: Unsupported depreciation stripping, inadequate economic substance, ineligible project timing, or unauthorized transaction-based compensation
platform_risks.impact: Tax assessments, recapture, investor losses, and fee disgorgement exposure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved tax opinion conditions and securities compliance exceptions
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend solicitation and closing, use appropriately licensed intermediaries, and restructure only as independently reviewed genuine equity ownership
